headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Uptrend holds, but the near-term mood is cautious

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's call is to scale up acquisition budget: the longer-term trend and the last three months both lean up, with medium confidence (67/100), so this is a reasonable time to fund growth, weighted toward channels that bring active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because the short-term mood is cautious, big funds have been pulling money out, and US inflation data plus the 27 October Fed meeting are near, grow the budget in steps rather than all at once and keep part of it flexible to pause if price closes below $81,218. This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a price call or trading advice.

reasons: Price is 16% above its 200-day average and up 31% over 90 days.
About 63% of the last 90 days closed above the long-term average.
Price sits about 3% above its 50-day average ($81,218), below the $86,603 30-day high.
The 200-day average still slopes down (-2%) and price is 33% below its record.
watch: The longer picture leans up, but big funds have been pulling money out and Fed officials keep talking about raising rates, while price rests only about 3% above its 50-day average ($81,218). A close below that line would test the uptrend; fund money returning and a move back above $86,603 would ease the worry.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger picture still points up, but this week people are holding back. Short term, the mood leans slightly cautious: big Bitcoin funds lost about $679M last week (CoinShares via PANews), and news is pulling the mood down a little after Ledger pulled its hardware wallets from shelves in Indonesia and nearby countries over a tampering scare (PANews). A close above $86,603 (the 30-day high) would turn this clearly up, a close below $81,218 (the 50-day average) turns it down, and in between expect choppy moves. Fund money flowing back in would firm this up; for now calm, trust-first messaging fits better than urgent pushes.

Over the next month the picture leans up with real strength: Bitcoin is about 31% higher than three months ago, and about six in ten of the last 90 days finished above the long-term average. Fewer people than usual are betting on a rise with borrowed money, so the climb does not look overstretched. There is room to climb if price gets above $86,603 (the 90-day high), while the move fades if it slips below $81,218 (the 50-day average), only about 3% under today's price. The Fed meets on 27 October and officials Collins and Williams have both pointed to more rate rises this year (PANews), so hotter inflation data would weaken this lean, while a calmer reading supports growth campaigns aimed at active traders.

On the 3-6 month view the recovery is intact but still young: price is about 16% above its 200-day average, though that average still slopes down slightly and Bitcoin is 33% below its record. Bank adoption news is adding a little: Russia's largest bank, Sberbank, won approval to offer Bitcoin and Ether trading from 1 December, and BNY and Citadel Securities settled a short-term loan deal using blockchain-recorded US Treasuries (both via PANews). The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,218 (the 200-day average), with $66,412 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. The 200-day average turning upward would strengthen this; for the business it supports steady investment in onboarding rather than short bursts.

team_notes.marketing: Keep growing, but calmly: the longer picture leans up while the short-term mood is cautious and no rally or drop window is open, so run steady campaigns for active traders rather than urgent pushes. Put trust and wallet-safety messages up front this week, since the Ledger tampering scare touches Indonesia directly.

items.why: Ledger has asked distributors in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong to pull its devices from shelves while it investigates suspected tampering, after German retailer MediaMarkt also suspended sales. Ledger says confirmed cases are limited to Southeast Asia so far; the cause and scale of losses are still under investigation.
items.marketing_angle: Directly relevant to Indonesian users: a timely moment for plain safety education on buying devices and protecting recovery phrases.

items.theme: Wall Street puts Treasuries on blockchains
items.why: BNY and Citadel Securities used blockchain-recorded US Treasuries in an overnight lending deal for the first time, settling in minutes. Ondo said its tokenized Treasuries passed $3 billion, with its USDY product overtaking BlackRock's BUIDL, and asset manager Federated Hermes plans on-chain fund shares next year.
items.marketing_angle: A good education topic on what 'tokenized' real-world assets are, for users curious beyond Bitcoin.
